subject: AIC comparison ; conditional or full likelihood when looking at sex differences

messages.author: 61ddffa51c481ed7
messages.subject: AIC comparison ; conditional or full likelihood when looking at sex differences
parts:
Hi,

I have a question about delta AIC when I have models that use sex as a covariate.

I read that there are many ways to model sex differences in secr, some using a conditional likelihood, others using the full likelihood; and that one must be careful and not mix these options when comparing AIC.

Models that do not look at sex differences, use a full likelihood (default setting in secr.fit(), CL = FALSE).

I assume that, models looking at sex differences, should also use a method with a full likelihood; isn't it important if planning to compare AIC afterwards?

Thanks very much
Kind regards, 

Elsa

messages.author: a962fffd7a5358b2
messages.subject: Re: AIC comparison ; conditional or full likelihood when looking at sex differences
parts:
Hi Elsa,
You can compare AIC values across models fitted with either likelihood, jut not across models that use different likelihoods.
If you use the conditional likelihood (CL = T), you can't model variation in density (except possibly across sessions). It's faster, and you can model sex as an individual covariate.
If you want to use the full likelihood, you can still fit models with sex effects, by modeling the different sexes as "groups" or "sessions".

Good luck,
Eric

A couple of footnotes (1) the 'hcov' formulation in the 'secr' package deals with unknown-sex animals (2) the need for sex-specific analyses is less than one would think, because of compensatory variation in detection parameters, but they are easy and satisfying, so Why not?
Murray
